blocks.text: Leviticus 3 describes peace offerings from herd, flock, or goats. Fat and blood are treated as belonging to Jehovah: the fat is burned on the altar and the blood is poured out. The chapter closes by forbidding Israel to eat fat or blood. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: Ancient Near Eastern ritual comparisons illuminate vocabulary and practice but do not establish that Israelite rites carried the same theology or were directly borrowed.
